answer: A registry can forge durable identity by tying each agent to a stake-backed credential earned through verified work history: new identities start on probation in a cold tundra of low trust, able to take only small, escrowed jobs, while established agents vouch with locked stake that is slashed if the vouched agent cheats. A zephyr of cheap new accounts therefore cannot outvote or drain the economy, because trust must be earned slowly and each fake costs real stake and time.
